title: Standings double-counts overlapping Brasileirão data: duplicate club rows and doubled game counts
evidence: src/lib.rs:316 standings() computes points from matches (not hardcoded, so R9's mechanism IS present), but src/lib.rs:331 groups by the raw team string with no normalization while Database::load (src/lib.rs:56 + src/lib.rs:90) concatenates Brasileirao_Matches.csv AND novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv — both labelled 'Brasileirão', both carrying all 380 rows of the 2019 Série A season, and find_matches' competition filter (src/lib.rs:218 contains()) matches both. Verified against the bundled data: the two files' 2019 team-name strings union to 39 distinct rows (only 'Botafogo-RJ' is byte-identical across both, so its counts add to 76 played on 38 real games; every other club splits into two rows, e.g. 'Flamengo-RJ' and 'Flamengo' each showing 38 played). standings(2019,'Brasileirão') therefore returns a 39-row table for a 20-team league.
suggestion: Dedup the two Brasileirão sources (or drop the overlapping seasons on load) and normalize the group-by key in standings() the same way same_team()/normalize() already do elsewhere. Add a standings test — it is the only query capability with no test.

title: All competition-wide Brasileirão aggregates double-count overlapping seasons
evidence: Same root cause as R9: Database::load concatenates Brasileirao_Matches.csv and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv with no dedup (src/lib.rs:56, src/lib.rs:90). statistics(Some('Brasileirão'), Some(2019)) (src/lib.rs:357) reports matches=760 and averages/biggest_win over the doubled set; team_record for a Brasileirão team in an overlapping season is likewise doubled. R10 only requires one aggregate stat computed over the data, so it still passes, but the numbers are wrong for the overlapping range.
suggestion: Fix once at load time by deduplicating the two Brasileirão files by (season, date, home, away).
